claims.statement: The Electron main process (electron/main.ts) is the only component that touches the filesystem, spawns a process, or calls LLM providers; the renderer reaches all of it exclusively through the preload bridge window.slr, with contextIsolation on, nodeIntegration off, and sandbox:true.

The renderer is treated as compromised-capable: each handler that takes a path, URL, ref, or argv-shaped value re-validates it in the main process, backed by session-only allowlists (knownProjectPaths, readablePdfPaths, writableExportPaths, knownGitRoots, allowedEscapes) populated only by native-dialog outcomes or successful first contact.
knownProjectPaths is populated by project:open/project:openPath on successful read and by project:pickSavePath/paths:sibling, and project:save refuses any path not in that set.

The BrowserWindow is created with preload.cjs, contextIsolation:true, nodeIntegration:false, sandbox:true; the window-state (size/position) is persisted to userData/window-state.json, reusing a saved position only if it still overlaps a connected display, and saving pre-maximize normal bounds.

createWindow resets allowClose and isQuitting to false at the top because on macOS the app outlives its last window; without the reset, a window closed via the unsaved-changes prompt would leave allowClose=true and a dock-reopened window would discard unsaved work without prompting.

The application menu routes Edit-menu Undo/Redo to the renderer via app:undo/app:redo (annotation history, not native text undo), omits View zoom roles so Ctrl +/-/0 reach the renderer for font scaling, and replaces the default Reload role with guardedReload so a reload is confirmed when there are unsaved changes.

External links are intercepted (setWindowOpenHandler denies new windows and hands target=_blank URLs to the default browser; will-navigate prevents navigation away from the app), and openExternalUrl restricts to http/https/mailto to avoid handing arbitrary schemes to the OS.

On app.whenReady, all permission requests (camera, mic, geolocation, notifications, etc.) are denied via setPermissionRequestHandler and setPermissionCheckHandler, since a window rendering untrusted PDFs has no legitimate use for them.

migrateLegacyUserData copies window-state.json and Local Storage from the pre-rename 'SLR Helper'/'slr-helper' profile into a never-used new profile before app.whenReady; an existing profile always wins over the old one.

The slr-file scheme is registered as privileged before the app is ready with corsEnabled:true, which is load-bearing because the renderer origin is not slr-file:// so PDF fetches are cross-origin; without corsEnabled Chromium rejects the request before protocol.handle runs.

The slr-file protocol handler carries the PDF path in the query (?path=<encoded>) rather than the URL path, because a '..' in a URL path is a dot-segment collapsed by URL parsing before the handler runs; getPdfSource in src/platform/electron.ts is the only builder of this URL.

resolveProjectPath is the single place PDF containment is checked and is shared by the slr-file handler and pdf:checkPath; it does a string containment check with path.resolve then a real-path check with realpath to catch symlinks inside the project directory, and allowedEscapes bypasses the boundary check for one reviewer-approved path.

allowedEscapes is session-only in memory, keyed by the exact stored relative path, cleared whenever projectDir changes to a different directory, and granted only by a native dialog in the main process (pdf:allowPath) so a compromised renderer cannot self-approve an escape.

Since v1.3 project annotations live in annotations/<paperId>/reviewer-<n>.json (or screening-<n>.json) plus consolidated/marks files; readProjectText reassembles the split layout into the legacy single-blob shape loadProject accepts, passing legacy single-file projects through untouched.

safeReadAnnotationFile and loadPaperFiles apply the same symlink-escape defense as resolveProjectPath (realpath containment), read only the file names this project's own kind owns, and treat corrupt JSON as absent rather than throwing; loadPaperFiles never reads the other project kind's files so a shared annotations/ folder cannot shadow this project's data.

writeProjectFiles is the single implementation of how a split project is written, shared by project:save and the git handlers (git:commitPartial, git:pullFinish); it reconciles the whole annotations/ folder to the files list, containment-checks each target twice (string and real-path), and assertNotSymlink refuses to write through a symlink.

pdf:read returns raw PDF bytes as Uint8Array (Buffer does not survive IPC) and is confined to readablePdfPaths (paths from native dialogs), unlike the slr-file protocol which is confined to the project directory.

pdf:embedMarks burns PdfMarks into real PDF annotation objects via pdf-lib's low-level PDFContext API (Highlights with QuadPoints, Text sticky notes), skips marks beyond the PDF's page count, appends to existing /Annots, and requires a new-file destination to be in writableExportPaths; writing over the original PDF target is exempt.

LLM API keys never enter the renderer: targets are stored in userData/llm-config.json (mode 0600) with the key encrypted via safeStorage; llm:configs returns only a hasKey boolean; llm:saveConfig keeps a stored key when an edit leaves the key blank; encryptKey refuses to write the key in the clear if safeStorage is unavailable.

llm:call substitutes the real key for the {{apiKey}} sentinel and sends via net.fetch (sidesteps CORS), checks the request URL's origin/scheme against the configured baseUrl, refuses redirects (redirect:'error') because provider key headers are not stripped by fetch, applies a 10-minute AbortController timeout, and llm:abort cancels an in-flight call by requestId.

Every git invocation uses execFile with an argument array and '--' before user-supplied paths/URLs, never a shell string, and never lets the renderer name argv; GIT_SAFE_CONFIG hard-overrides dangerous config keys (core.fsmonitor, core.hooksPath, protocol.ext, etc.) because a received project folder brings its own .git/.

runGit strips inherited GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/etc., sets GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and GIT_EDITOR=true (no tty; credential helpers and SSH agents are left untouched), treats non-zero exit as data not an exception, and uses 30s/900s timeouts with a 32MB maxBuffer.

assertRoot guards every root-taking git handler against knownGitRoots (populated by git:info and git:clone), and assertRelPath/assertRef re-check renderer-supplied paths and refs through rules in src/git/relpath.ts and src/git/ref.ts (kept in src/ so the vitest suite can reach them).

Native self-update is Windows/Linux only; macOS is excluded because electron-updater's Squirrel.Mac path needs a notarized Developer ID signature this project doesn't pay for, so mac keeps the check-only banner. autoDownload and autoInstallOnAppQuit are both false, so download/install only happen on explicit update:download/update:install calls; update:check is a no-op on darwin.

Because there is no code-signing certificate for Windows/Linux, electron-updater's sha512 check only catches transport corruption; verifyUpdateFeed independently fetches the feed file plus its .sig and verifies an Ed25519 signature (verifyReleaseSignature against RELEASE_PUBLIC_KEY_B64 baked into the app) before update:download calls autoUpdater.downloadUpdate(), chaining trust: signature covers the feed, electron-updater's sha512 covers the installer against the trusted feed.

scripts/sign-release.cjs signs each electron-updater feed file (latest.yml/latest-linux.yml) with the project Ed25519 private key (RELEASE_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY GitHub Actions secret, never committed) and writes <feed>.sig, which the release workflow attaches alongside the feed.

src/model/version.ts provides a check-only update banner used on all platforms (including mac): it calls the GitHub releases API, fails silently on 404/403/network error (repo may be private; embedding a token would leak), runs on every startup, caches for 15 minutes, and pickInstaller selects the asset matching the machine.

The preload bridge exposes the SlrBridge interface mirrored in src/platform/electron.ts (ElectronAdapter implements PlatformAdapter over it); it includes os info, project/pdf/text/paths operations, the full git surface, self-update, and deliberately no way to read an LLM API key back.

Quit/unsaved-changes coordination spans the process boundary: the renderer keeps isDirty informed via app:setDirty; before-quit sets isQuitting; the close handler intercepts when dirty and shows a native Save/Don't Save/Cancel dialog; Save sends app:requestSave, the renderer saves and replies app:saveComplete(ok), and on ok the main process resumes the quit else aborts it and keeps the window open.

useElectronCloseGuard wires the Electron menu/lifecycle integration: it treats either an unsaved annotation project or an open project-editor draft as dirty, pushes dirty state on every change, routes onRequestSave and Edit-menu Undo/Redo to whichever store is on screen, and forwards self-update progress events to the store.

ClosePrompt.tsx is the in-app analogue for closing a project (not the app) with unsaved changes, mirroring the native Electron quit dialog's three choices and wording, resolved through useStore.resolveClosePrompt so closing a project and quitting behave alike.

electron/main.ts imports only shared pure logic from src/ (git url/path/ref/output modules, model project/pdfMarks/pdfExport/updateSignature) which import nothing DOM-specific, so they typecheck under both the main process's node types and the renderer's DOM types and remain reachable by the vitest suite.
